newsitem.title: USA: Salomon sees good trends in place for small-caps.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees good trends in place for small-caps.

text.p: Salomon Brothers head of quantitative research Eric Sorensen says small-cap stocks could be poised for some solid performance in the coming months and could outperform other major indices, based on recent strength of the dollar, attractive valuations, and expectations for a strong January.
"Currently in the United States, we believe the scope for small-cap outperformance has significantly improved," Sorensen said in a statement.

Small-cap stocks have historically returned a 200 basis point premium over large cap stocks but have lagged lately, he said, with the Standard & Poor's 500 Index outperforming the Russell 2000 index of small-cap stocks by about 1000 basis points over the past six months.

Sorensen said the dollar's strong performance, which aids small-cap stocks by reducing the relative earnings growth of multinational companies, and attractive relative valuations are favorable trends in place that could help small-cap's performance. He said Salomon's forecast of less volatility in the stock market would also benefit the sector.
Sorensen also cited "the January effect". "Since 1926, during the month of January, small-cap stocks have dramatically outperformed large-cap stocks.

Given current attractive valuation levels for small-caps and a steepening of the yield curve over the last year -- two historical predictors of a strong January effect -- Salomon expects that January will warm up to small-cap investors to a larger-than-average extent," he said.
